fieldOverrides.__comment__: Event bodies are opaque pointers, never queried. Exempting them from indexing removes an index entry per body field per event, which is both a storage cost and a write-latency cost on every append.

The projects index queries collectionGroup('members').where('uid','==',me) — the only way a browser can list its own projects, since rules reject a list of /projects rather than filtering it. Automatic single-field indexes are COLLECTION-scoped only, so the COLLECTION_GROUP entry must be declared explicitly or production answers FAILED_PRECONDITION. The emulator does not enforce indexes at all, so the conformance suite passes without this and only production reveals it.

connect() finds an invite by collectionGroup("invites").where("code_sha256","==",hash) — it cannot know which project the code belongs to until it finds it. Same trap as members.uid: automatic single-field indexes are COLLECTION-scoped only, so production answered FAILED_PRECONDITION while the emulator, which does not enforce indexes at all, was happy. Found by reading the api function log, not by testing.

__comment__: readEvents is a single-field range+order on `seq`, served by the automatic single-field index. No composite index is required, which is why `indexes` is empty rather than unwritten.
